title: Bob Scobey calls him to Chicago in 1959
summary: Hodes recalls Scobey phoning him in 1959 to replace Tut Soper. He joined for a few days.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: And then work, whatever I could and then what saved me was in 1959, Bob Scobey came to town and called me. Now, I had bad recollections of Scobey from the Lou Waters band. So when he called me, I was visiting my daughter. And I says, no, I don't read that good to read your charts. I'm not interested in joining a band. But he had Tut Soper, and Tut, again, had done something in the band that they wanted him to leave yesterday, for some reason. I don't know what he did. I don't blame it on his playing because I always thought, if he wanted to, he could play like Earl Hines, on that style.
He can play more like Earl Hines than Earl Hines can. ... piano player I ever played with.

Yeah. I thought he could be excellent, yeah. So they wanted to get rid of him right away, that night. So Bob just brushed away every one of my remarks. Says, you don't have to look at the music, just sit at the piano and if you know the tune, play it. If you don't know it, lay out. You don't have to do nothing, just show up, please.
I couldn't say no. So I came. It's the luckiest thing I ever did. I went there and I played, the arrangements I could read I read.
